title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Unsloth GGUF on llama.cpp, DGX Spark
slug_note: The plain Q4_K_M of the 35B-A3B MoE on the Spark: 66 tok/s, 23 GiB — the baseline lane against the MTP and Ollama rows.

variation.revision_note: HF snapshot resolved and served on the Spark during the 2026-10-27 test

requirements.notes: Measured on a DGX Spark (2026-10-27): 23.2 GiB dropped from MemAvailable with the recipe as written (--ctx-size 8192).

steps.text: Install llama.cpp (see Step 0 in Quick start). On Ubuntu / DGX OS install libssl-dev first, or -hf cannot download.

measurements.method: openai_bench.py: streaming /v1/chat/completions, single stream, one warm-up discarded, fresh nonce per summarise prompt (cold prefill), decode = (completion_tokens-1)/(last-first token time), temperature 0.6, median of 3; summarise neutral filler (633-token prompt, 256-512 output tokens)

drop in MemAvailable from before start (OS file cache dropped) to server ready; llama-server build 11866 (commit 3f03b1772) with --ctx-size 8192

caveats: Works as written on a DGX Spark (2026-10-27): `llama-server -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:Q4_K_M --ctx-size 8192 -ngl 99` — llama.cpp build 11866 (commit 3f03b1772); server ready 30 s after start with the OS file cache dropped; the functional check passed; MemAvailable dropped 23.2 GiB (weights + KV at --ctx-size 8192).

Same checkpoint family as the Ollama qwen3.6:35b-a3b lane measured on the Spark on 2026-10-26 (90.5 tok/s short prompt at Ollama's 262,144-token default context): llama.cpp here ran at 8,192 context for comparability with the rest of the queue, so the two rows are not a fair engine A/B (different context, different resident KV).
